headline: MCP TypeScript SDK v1 to v2: A Migration Guide
description: Migrate from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk to the v2 packages: the codemod, the package split, the Zod 4.2 trap that fails silently, renamed errors and context, removed transports, and why adopting 2026-07-28 is a separate decision.
keywords: MCP TypeScript SDK v2 migration, @modelcontextprotocol/server, @modelcontextprotocol/client, MCP codemod, Zod 4 Standard Schema, registerTool, ProtocolError, SdkHttpError, StreamableHTTPServerTransport, serveStdio, createMcpHandler, MCP breaking changes

about.name: MCP TypeScript SDK v2
about.description: Major SDK revision replacing the monolithic @modelcontextprotocol/sdk package with split server, client, core, and adapter packages

about.name: MCP codemod
about.description: The @modelcontextprotocol/codemod tool that mechanically applies v1-to-v2 import, symbol, and call-shape rewrites and marks sites it cannot safely change

about.name: Standard Schema
about.description: Schema interface specification adopted for v2 tool and prompt schemas, requiring Zod 4, Valibot, ArkType, or another compatible library

about.name: Zod 4
about.description: Required schema library major for SDK v2; version 4.2.0 or later self-converts to JSON Schema and preserves .describe() field descriptions

about.name: Protocol revision 2026-07-28
about.description: Stateless MCP protocol revision that v2 can serve, opted into per entry point rather than enabled by upgrading the SDK

about.name: Streamable HTTP transport
about.description: The remaining HTTP transport in v2, split into Node and web-standard runtime variants after SSEServerTransport was removed

about.name: structuredContent
about.description: Tool result field widened from an object type to unknown in v2, requiring narrowing before property access and an explicit undefined presence check

mainEntity.name: Do I have to migrate to MCP TypeScript SDK v2 by July 28, 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. July 28, 2026 is when the 2026-07-28 specification text publishes, not a switch-off for anything. Existing clients and servers keep working. The v1.x SDK line remains supported with bug fixes and security updates for at least six months after v2 ships stable.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading to MCP TypeScript SDK v2 change what my server puts on the wire?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and this is the key property of the migration. A hand-constructed Server or McpServer on v2 speaks the same 2025-era protocol it spoke on v1. Serving the 2026-07-28 revision requires explicitly moving to createMcpHandler for HTTP or serveStdio for stdio.

mainEntity.name: Is MCP TypeScript SDK v2 ESM-only?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, although early beta announcements described it that way. v2 is ESM-first but ships a CommonJS build alongside ESM, so CommonJS projects can require the packages directly without a dynamic import shim. It requires Node.js 20 or newer and runs on Node, Bun, and Deno.

mainEntity.name: Why does my MCP server start fine and then fail on the first tools/list after migrating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zod 3. A Zod 3 range that satisfied the v1 peer dependency installs and typechecks cleanly under v2, then the first tools/list answers with an error pointing at fromJsonSchema() while the process keeps running. Check the declared range in package.json rather than the installed version and bump to zod ^4.2.0.

mainEntity.name: What does the MCP codemod not handle that will actually cause problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three things. The Zod version, which is a pre-flight fix rather than a rewrite. Files that receive SDK surfaces through dependency injection and therefore have no imports to rewrite, where v1 idioms fail at runtime rather than compile time. And behavioral changes with no rename attached, such as structuredContent narrowing and the switch to a 2020-12 JSON Schema validator default.

mainEntity.name: Can I migrate a monorepo to MCP TypeScript SDK v2 one package at a time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is the recommended approach. Run the codemod against each member directory, since the manifest summary is computed from that member's own imports. For a workspace pinned to Zod 3, add a zod-v4 alias dependency resolving to zod ^4.2.0 in only the migrating member and author SDK-bound schemas with it.
